newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian fires deliberately lit, say police.
newsitem.headline: Australian fires deliberately lit, say police.

text.p: Forest fires that ravaged the outskirts of Australia's second biggest city, killing three people and razing over 40 homes, were started deliberately, police in Melbourne said on Thursday.
Police reacted with disbelief as they released the findings of an exhaustive forensic investigation of the burnt-out homes in heavily wooded mountains in Melbourne's outer east.
"We've conducted exhaustive forensic investigations and we have eliminated the possibility of an accidental cause of these fires," arson squad spokesman Adrian Edwards said.
"I think one only has to look at the devastation and the despair that's been left behind and it's very hard to comprehend that a person could commit such an act," he added.
Three people died in the fires, which broke out during the city's worst heatwaves in a decade in Melbourne's urbanised Dandenong mountains.
A couple aged 26 and 24 and their neighbour, a 50-year-old woman, died after they took shelter from the blaze in a cellar in the couple's home.
The house burnt down around them and their charred remains were found side by side on Wednesday, as firefighters and police mopped up after rain helped extinguish the fires.
Police suspect up to five separate fires were deliberately lit in the space of an hour in the Dandenong district on Tuesday.
"It's possible that one person using a mode of transport could have been at all five places," Edwards said.
The fires were among an outbreak of 10 major forest fires across Victoria state early this week, when hot winds and soaring temperatures left woodland tinder dry.
The fires recalled memories of Ash Wednesday in summer 1983, when 76 people died and over 2,400 houses burnt to the ground in fires in Victoria and the neighbouring state of South Australia.
